transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-11
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Arnett (Redwood CSM), Leah Ortiz (Aurionix), Devon Park (Aurionix), Anika Bose (Aurionix TPM)
Recording note: auto-generated transcript; moderate noise; some proper nouns mis-transcribed.

--- Optional auto-summary (auto):
Maya: quick recap and objective - align on close plan and who owns what.

00:00:12 - Maya: Hi everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:00:15 - Leah: Yep loud and clear, hey Maya thanks.
00:00:22 - Devon: Morning/afternoon, we're excited to move this to close.
00:00:30 - Maya: Cool, goal for today is to walk through the crescendo close play, pricing delta between hosted and dedicated, and finalize who owns the partner handoff. Samir will cover the benchmark asks. Jules on ops handoff.

00:01:05 - Samir: quick note - the benchmark we ran yesterday was a lightweight sim, not production, so we'll need to do a partner-facing run with Aurionix data shape to be meaningful.
00:01:20 - Anika: yeah we have a sample prompt set and a couple of spike workloads we can share, mostly 2-8k context.

00:02:03 - Maya: perfect. First question for Aurionix - what's the buying center and timeline? Devon?
00:02:15 - Devon: We're looking to close by end of March ideally. CRO wants to see a commercial delta and risks mapped. Procurement wants SOC2 + basic KMS and EU data residency for some customers, but first deal is US-only.

00:03:00 - Leah: also need to understand partner commission mechanics - we typically co-sell with a 15-20% referral fee, but need clarity on whether Redwood will support partner crediting and joint invoicing.
00:03:22 - Maya: good call, we'll include options in the close-plan deck. We have a partner rebate flow and can do partner-managed invoices for Dedicated, we'll surface that.

00:04:10 - Samir: tech note - Dedicated offers isolation and predictable throughput, but cost-per-token is higher if you underutilize. Hosted gives bursty cost but lower unit price for small volumes. For your 10-20k monthly tokens pilot, hosted might be cheaper to start.
00:04:45 - Anika: what's the latency delta? Our customers are latency-sensitive for chat agents.
00:05:00 - Samir: ballpark p50 is similar for similar instance types, p95 can drift on hosted depending on shared load; Dedicated provides more consistent p95. We'll quantify with numbers.

00:06:10 - Devon: competition check - Anthropic ran a pilot with one of our mid-market customers and Vertex's managed endpoint is in eval. We need a clear commercial + technical story to beat them.

00:06:40 - Maya: understoood. part of the close play is a 'win-back' reference sheet and 2-week tech spike with an exec readout.

00:07:20 - Jules: ops handoff idea: once deal enters committed, Redwood partner success will run a 30-day onboarding checklist (kickoff, creds, basic routing, SLA paperwork). I'll map the steps and share a timeline.

00:07:45 - Leah: do you have a sample SOW or onboarding doc we can show the CRO?
00:07:53 - Jules: yes I'll attach the onboarding SOW in the deck.

00:08:30 - Maya: pricing. we've prepared two starter packages: hosted starter and dedicated starter. Hosted: per token pricing with monthly commitment; Dedicated: reserved capacity with monthly minimum. For this pilot, we can show a blended first-quarter price to make numbers comparable.
00:09:00 - Devon: can you include an option where Aurionix receives partner credits tied to invoice milestones?
00:09:12 - Maya: yes, we'll include a partner-credit structure.

00:09:45 - Samir: regarding benchmarks - what we need from you: 1) sample prompt set 2) traffic pattern (concurrency, qps) 3) success metric (p50, p95, tokens per sec, cost per 1k tokens). If you share those, we can run a runbook and return numbers.
00:10:20 - Anika: we'll send prompt set and a small synthetic trace by EOD tomorrow.

00:11:00 - Maya: risk lanes: procurement timeline, data residency for EU, and references. Leah, can you surface the buyer persona and procurement stakeholders?
00:11:20 - Leah: yes procurement lead is Marko, I'll introduce. He cares about encryption at rest, KMS, and audit logs.
00:11:35 - Maya: great, we have SOC2 and KMS integrations; we'll share the security pack. Note sometimes the auto-doc calls it Redwood Dedicate instead of Redwood Dedicated - ignore the small text issues.

00:12:10 - Devon: our legal will want to see SLA and liability caps. Are those negotiable?
00:12:22 - Jules: we have standard SLAs for uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated. For Hosted we have different SLOs. We can bubble up DL and see if we can offer a higher SLA for this account as an attach.

00:13:00 - Samir: technical deep dive - for the spike we'll recommend a quantization profile that balances cost & quality, and we can try a lightweight batching config. For 8k contexts we need to watch memory.

00:13:40 - Anika: memory and token limits were the reason we paused a previous vendor. Can you demo how you handle prefix caching?
00:13:53 - Samir: yes in the spike we'll enable KV prefix caching and show token reuse benefits. There's some ops work to configure but we can script it.

00:14:30 - Maya: let's talk timeline steps in order: (1) Redwood sends joint close-plan deck + benchmark ask (2) Aurionix shares prompt set and stakeholders (3) Redwood runs benchmark and returns numbers (4) Exec readout + final commercial. Does that alignment work?
00:14:54 - Leah: yes that sequence works.

00:15:30 - Devon: one more thing on the partner economics - we need clarity on co-sell logos and case study rights. We typically require a 90-day embargo before public case study.
00:15:45 - Maya: we'll note that in the agreement.

00:16:10 - Samir: small but important note: if you choose Dedicated and want on-prem routing for EU customers, there are two options: Redwood Private (VPC) or partner-managed on-prem. Both add ops lead time. We'll map the delta in the deck.
00:16:40 - Anika: likely for now we stick US-only, EU is a later expansion.

00:17:10 - Maya: objections we expect from your procurement/IT: encryption, audit logs, and data residency. We'll prepare a brief mapping doc showing how Redwood meets each requirement.
00:17:30 - Leah: good.

00:18:05 - Devon: on reps and warranties - we may ask for indemnities around data leakage. Is that standard?
00:18:20 - Jules: we include data protection clauses in our standard EULA; heavy edits may require legal review. We can surface the base language.

00:19:00 - Maya: let's talk commercial levers for win: 1) 3-month blended rate 2) joint marketing budget 3) faster onboarding commitment from Redwood. Which of those would move the needle?
00:19:25 - Devon: blended rate + faster onboarding are big. Joint marketing helps for longer tail.
00:19:40 - Leah: joint marketing also helps us displace Anthropic references.

00:20:10 - Samir: technical ask for the benchmark: what model family do you want us to use? An open Llama-like model or a smaller LLM equivalent?
00:20:26 - Anika: we want something representative of what we'll ship, Llama 2 family is fine for the spike.
00:20:35 - Samir: good. We'll run Llama2-70B quantized sim with the sample prompts. That will give a fair apples-to-apples.

00:21:10 - Maya: governance note - we'll include a single-row timeline in the deck with owners for each milestone. Also propose weekly standups during the tech spike.
00:21:30 - Leah: weekly check-ins appreciated.

00:22:00 - Devon: procurement ramp - our procurement folks will want to see a PoP and proof of processing separation for partner data.
00:22:12 - Maya: we have a data processing addendum template we'll attach.

00:23:00 - Samir: ops detail - if we demo a 2-week spike, we can show p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens plus a sample prompt-level fidelity score. That should be enough for the CRO to greenlight.
00:23:24 - Devon: that's the ask.

00:24:00 - Maya: any blockers on the Aurionix side to running the spike in the next two weeks?
00:24:08 - Anika: we need to confirm ec2-like credentials for test data transfer, but should be OK. I'll get ops to approve.
00:24:20 - Leah: we'll aim to have all artifacts to you by Thursday.

00:25:00 - Maya: ok good. Now a quick discussion on partner attribution - do you want to pursue joint logos or pure referral?
00:25:12 - Leah: joint logo is preferred; they help our GTM. If there's revenue share, we may accept referral.
00:25:30 - Maya: we'll map both options in the pricing worksheet.

00:26:10 - Samir: slight tangent - for multi-tenant workflows we can turn on per-tenant routing and prefix caching. There's a small config cost, but in pilots it usually pays off in token savings.
00:26:38 - Anika: sounds promising.

00:27:05 - Devon: procurement also flagged the need for a backup provider in case of downtime. Is Redwood ok to publish a fallback plan?
00:27:18 - Jules: yes, we have fallbacks: model variant routing and multi-region failover. We'll include an operations runbook excerpt.

00:28:00 - Maya: let's capture the main risks and mitigations (quick list): procurement timeline -> offer 60-day pilot and accelerated SOW; data residency -> roadmap to Private/VPC; references -> partner-provided case and Redwood-managed reference if needed.

00:28:40 - Anika: that works.

00:29:10 - Samir: I'm going to outline the benchmark plan now: deliverable table with metrics, scripts, and results. We'll deliver an initial report and a follow-up deep dive.

00:29:40 - Maya: commercial note - if we need to move faster on pricing we can offer a one-time credit if committed by Feb 28. Is that something that helps?
00:29:55 - Devon: yes that will help accelerate internal approvals.

00:30:30 - Leah: one more stakeholder: our channel legal requires a partner play agreement; can you share a template?
00:30:40 - Jules: yes will attach partner play agreement template to the deck.

00:31:15 - Maya: ok we'll lock on action items. Recap: Maya sends deck and pricing worksheet (due 2/14), Samir runs benchmarks (due 2/18), Leah confirms exec sponsor and procurement intro (due 2/17), Jules schedules partner ops intro (due 2/16).

00:31:40 - Devon: good. Quick clarifying Q - are there any minimum commit timeframes if we go Dedicated?
00:31:50 - Maya: Dedicated is typically monthly reserved capacity with a 3 or 6 month commit by default but we can propose a 90-day pilot reserve at reduced effective rate.

00:32:20 - Anika: will you include a waterfall that shows how unit cost evolves with token volume?
00:32:30 - Samir: yes cost curves will be in the pricing sheet.

00:33:00 - Maya: communications plan - once we have benchmark numbers we'll do a 30-minute exec readout for the CRO and bring in partner success.

00:33:20 - Leah: we'll block time that week.

00:33:40 - (brief cross-talk / laughter)

00:34:10 - Samir: technical caveat - when benchmarking open models, exact parity with Anthropic isn't possible; but we'll aim to show cost/perf delta for your workload.
00:34:36 - Devon: understood.

00:35:10 - Maya: any final questions before we call it?
00:35:18 - Leah: no, thanks, I think we're aligned.
00:35:25 - Devon: thumbs up.
00:35:30 - Anika: quick note - I'll send the prompt set and a short synthetic trace to Samir tonight.

00:36:00 - Maya: great. Jules you'll schedule the partner ops intro?
00:36:05 - Jules: yep will send calendar invite for 2/16.

00:36:40 - Maya: ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck and the ask doc.
00:36:48 - (meeting winds down small talk)

00:37:30 - END OF TRANSCRIPT (remaining time used for private sidebars not recorded cleanly).

Notes/References:
- Deck link placeholder: https://drive.google.com/joint-close-plan-AURIONIX (to be shared)
- Benchmark worksheet: link to pricing sheet (google sheets) will be attached by Maya.
- Security pack: link to SOC2/KMS docs to be attached by Jules.

Audio/transcript quirks: 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'Redwood Dedicatee', 'Llama2' occasionally 'Llama two', 'KV cache' sometimes 'kV cache'.

Recap (auto): Main outcome is alignment on a time-boxed spike, a pricing worksheet with partner crediting, and an ops handoff to partner success. Next steps captured as action items above.
